newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar drops vs yen in Tokyo on exporters' sales.
newsitem.headline: Dollar drops vs yen in Tokyo on exporters' sales.

text.p: 0640 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar fell against the yen by late Tokyo on Tuesday on heavy sales by Japanese exporters and profit-taking, but the greenback's falls were limited due to its healthy fundamentals, dealers said.
"Exporters were selling heavily since early trade, weighing on the dollar, but despite such selling it has been well-supported," a Japanese city bank dealer said.
The dollar was put under downward pressure against the yen since early trade on a series of comments on trade issues.
Remarks by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky that the U.S. automotive trade deficit with Japan is getting worse capped the dollar's gains against the yen.
"There is no question that Japan has stalled on deregulation in this (the auto) sector. That is of significant concern and inexcusable," Barshefsky told Reuters.
Japanese Trade Minister Shinji Sato said that the recent rise in Japan's trade surplus is temporary, although trade tensions may rise if the surplus does not fall in the autumn.
"I believe it is a temporary problem, although I realise that if the trade surplus does not come down in the autumn, it will be a tough situation," Sato told reporters on Tuesday.

Dealers said the market was also reluctant to buy the dollar aggressively above the 200-day moving average of around 117.97 yen. In addition, overseas operators were said to be keen to sell dollars just below 118 yen to avoid hitting options positions likely placed above that point.
"With strong technical resistance and rumours of options-related sales, the market was unable to test the dollar/yen upside in Tokyo," a Japanese trust bank dealer said.

The dollar also suffered because of sales by Japanese institutional investors, but the dollar was firmly protected above 117 yen on short-covering and on expectations that Japanese trust banks and U.S. operators would be keen to pick up dollars on dips, dealers said.
Dealers said that the dollar was more likely to test a key technical point of 119.00 yen in the near term, the 50-percent retracement of the 1997 high/low move from 126.47 to 110.62.
Dealers said the dollar's uptrend could speed up and test that point if it can break through 118.10 yen, where stop-loss buy orders are rumoured to be placed.
In the dollar/mark trade, profit-taking dragged down the dollar below 1.84 marks, and mark buying in crosses against yen also weighed on the greenback.
Dealers said position-adjustment dollar sales for marks were detected after the dollar reached 1.8490 marks overnight, its highest since November 1989.
The dollar closed at 117.78/88 yen and 1.8415/25 marks in New York on Monday.
Sterling was little changed at $1.6332/42 by late Tokyo after plunging sharply overnight. It closed at $1.6335/45 in New York on Monday.

Former Japanese Vice Finance Minister Makoto Utsumi said that a range of 110-120 yen to the dollar is not a problem for Japan but a yen weaker than 125 yen to the greenback would be excessive, but the market ignored his remarks.

The mark/yen rebounded from its lows back to around the previous New York close due to purchases by overseas operators, but it was capped on selling interest by exporters before 64 yen. The mark stood at 63.94/97 yen by late Tokyo.
